subject: business-studies
title: Product Life Cycle Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll trace the product life cycle, calculate market share and pick extension strategies.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies — product life cycle stages, market share calculations and extension strategies.
final_note: You can identify life-cycle stages, calculate market share, and choose extension strategies.

concepts.def: Launch stage — low sales, heavy promotion costs
Sales rising fast, profits start to flow
Peak sales, competition strong, profits stable
Sales falling — withdraw or extend the product
Tactic to delay decline (new market, redesign)
Firm sales / total market sales x 100

walkthroughs.body_html:
Most products travel through Introduction → Growth → Maturity → Decline.

Each stage needs different marketing — heavy promotion at launch, defending share at maturity, cutting costs in decline.

Market share = (your sales / total market sales) × 100.

If you sell £2m in a £20m market, your share is 10%. Tracking it tells you if you're winning or losing.

Extension strategies delay decline.

Examples: redesign/relaunch (new packaging), find new markets (export), add features, change advertising, drop the price.

options: Introduction
Growth
Maturity
Decline

options: Cutting wages
Repackaging a product
Hiring more cleaners
Issuing new shares

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A brand is the company that makes a product.
The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
A brand is just the logo on a product.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
